clue.text: Maybe Meghan expected endless battle with Queen and her allies?

indicators.note: endless says the word for expected loses its final letter

parts.note: a baby or bill that is expected is due

parts.words: battle with Queen and her allies
parts.note: chess is a war game fought with a queen alongside her king, bishops, knights and so on

explanation.surface: A tabloid hint that Meghan foresees a never-ending feud with the Queen and the rest of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter from DUE. The royal battle on the surface is really a game on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Meghan Markle holds the title Duchess of Sussex, so she is one example of the rank.

clue.text: Essentially, lunch ain't free

indicators.note: essentially points to the inside of the words that follow, where the answer sits without their outer letters

explanation.surface: The old saying that there is no such thing as a free lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes the core of 'lunch ain't', dropping the outer L and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something chained up is to release its shackles, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Spotted killer's desire to break into laugh

indicators.note: one word breaking into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: ha is the written sound of a laugh
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A murderer with a spotty record feels an urge to burst out laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break into' is the container signal. The spotted hyena is famous for its laughing call, so the laugh in the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is an African predator with a dappled coat, so it is literally a spotted killer.

clue.text: Posh Spice dancing for fans

indicators.note: letters dancing move about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Victoria Beckham, the Spice Girl called Posh, performing a dance routine for her fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges FORFANS. 'Posh Spice' is not the pop star but an upmarket seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron, made from crocus stigmas, is the world's most expensive seasoning, hence a luxurious one.

clue.text: Perhaps Y-fronts of Uncle Neil keep nothing concealed these days

indicators.note: concealed means one string is tucked away inside the other
fronts of takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

parts.note: these days means at present, now

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of Uncle Neil's underpants, which nowadays hide nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fronts of' gives UNKN from Uncle, Neil, keep, nothing; 'concealed' puts NOW between the K and the last N. The Y of 'Y-fronts' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra x, y and z stand for variables to be found, so a letter Y is a classic example of one.

clue.text: Forget it's a way to bid at auction with reserve

parts.words: a way to bid at auction
parts.note: a bidder in a saleroom can signal with a nod of the head
ice is coolness or reserve of manner

explanation.surface: An auction-room tip: forget it, you can bid with a quiet nod while staying restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with reserve' sounds like an auction reserve price, but reserve here is chilly restraint, ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: No dice is an informal refusal or admission of failure, the same as saying forget it.

clue.text: Senseless row on the phone with Charlie

parts.note: numb means without feeling or sensation

indicators.note: on the phone signals a word as heard rather than seen

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat with oars

explanation.surface: A pointless argument conducted over the telephone with someone named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senseless' looks like the definition, but Charlie is: British slang for a fool. 'on the phone' turns SCULL into SKULL.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal speech a charlie is a silly person, the same as a dimwit or blockhead.

clue.text: Pretty women's pants worn by Raider

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters before it are a mess to be rearranged

parts.note: the setter Raider refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to wearing women's underwear, which apparently look pretty on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is the anagram signal on WOMENS plus I, the setter speaking of himself; 'worn by' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome describes charming, appealing looks, a fairly close match for pretty as an adjective.

clue.text: Movements are more comfortable with this seat cushion?

definitions.text: Movements are more comfortable with this

definitions.meaning: read literally, something that makes a stool softer

explanation.definitionFit: A stool softener is a laxative, and the phrase can whimsically describe padding that softens a stool or seat.

clue.text: Point of no return after lodging new complaint

indicators.note: after lodging means once the next item has been housed inside it

parts.note: in tennis an ace is a serve that wins the point with no return

explanation.surface: Someone files a fresh complaint having reached the point where there is no going back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point of no return' sounds like an irreversible stage but is a tennis ace; 'after lodging' places N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean a medical ailment, and spotty skin is a common one.

clue.text: American pianist working on sad motif

indicators.note: letters set working are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician from the USA developing a melancholy musical theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ONSADMOTIF.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats Domino was the New Orleans rhythm-and-blues pianist behind Blueberry Hill.

clue.text: Some might say strange but fair

indicators.note: some might say signals a word spoken that matches another in sound

parts.note: bizarre means strange or odd

explanation.surface: A grudging verdict: odd, perhaps, but fair-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' is the noun, a market, not the adjective; 'Some might say' admits the sound match is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a market or charity sale, the same kind of event as a fete or fair.

clue.text: Pretext for celebration

definitions.meaning: an ... can be a reason or excuse for doing something

explanation.surface: An excuse to throw a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasion means both a cause or excuse and a notable event marked with festivities.

clue.text: Glasses balanced so precisely

definitions.meaning: spectacles rest perched across the bridge of the face

explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles sit literally there, and the idiom means exactly, as in a guess that is spot on.

clue.text: Clumsy handler is unlucky

indicators.note: clumsy suggests letters fumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: A clumsy handler simply had bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsy' rearranges HANDLERIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard lines is a British expression of sympathy meaning bad luck, so it fits unlucky as an exclamation.

clue.text: Potter about, right before last of weed's smoked?

indicators.note: about here means going round the next item

parts.note: a snooker cue is what pots the balls

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Harry Potter or a dawdler lighting up some weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter about' looks like dawdling, but a potter is a cue. 'about' puts R inside CUE; 'last of' takes D from weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish or bacon that is smoked has been preserved, which is what cured means.

clue.text: Play piano in class

indicators.note: in places the item before it inside the next

parts.note: a sort is a kind or class
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A child playing the piano during a school lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb about the piano, and 'class' looks like school; 'in' puts P inside SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport means play or fun, as in doing something just for sport.

clue.text: Begin official march outside

indicators.note: outside means the second word wraps round the first

parts.note: to pace is to march or stride
a ref is a referee, a match official

explanation.surface: Instructions to start an official parade or protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begin' is a verb here, as in prefacing a talk; 'outside' is the container signal, wrapping the march round the official.
explanation.definitionFit: To preface something is to introduce or open it, so it serves as a verb for begin.

clue.text: Arranged a free lift for final destination?

indicators.note: arranged means these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone organises a free ride to wherever the trip ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges AFREELIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven or the hereafter is where many believe the soul ends up, so it is everyone's last stop.

clue.text: Den crawling with mice found locally

indicators.note: letters crawling around one another are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A burrow swarming with rodents, a common sight in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawling with' rearranges DENMICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease or species is native to and confined to a particular region.

clue.text: Day's social gathering provides entertainment for tossers?

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday, with the possessive adding S
a bee is a gathering for work and company, like a sewing bee

explanation.surface: A day's party provides fun for some rude-sounding people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossers' is a British insult, but here it simply means people who throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisbee is a plastic disc flung back and forth for fun, entertainment for throwers.

clue.text: Chicken crossing a road? Step on it

indicators.note: one word crossing another here means it surrounds it

parts.note: a hen is a female chicken
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: The old joke of a chicken crossing the road, told to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' is the container signal: the bird goes across, around, the road with its article.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom urging speed, the same as telling someone to hurry.

clue.text: Someone to pass time with?

parts.note: looks like a companion for idle hours, but time here is a prison sentence

explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner sharing your cell keeps you company while you serve your sentence.

clue.text: Rubbish teacher facing the sack after recession

indicators.note: after recession means once it has receded, read backwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
the sack is slang for bed

explanation.surface: A teacher fired as the economy shrinks feels thrown out like trash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sack' looks like dismissal but is bed; 'after recession' turns SIRBED around.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or wreckage left behind.

clue.text: Suddenly run right in front of woman

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

parts.note: a woman's bust is her chest

explanation.surface: Someone darts abruptly into the path of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of woman' looks like a first-letter pick but means her chest; 'in' puts R inside BUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst into a room is to rush in abruptly, a sudden run.

clue.text: Standard PowerPoint template's first 500 pages

parts.note: a power point is a socket for the mains electricity

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Office talk about a standard slide template that runs to hundreds of pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PowerPoint' looks like the software but is an electric socket, the mains.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream means normal or conventional, the standard that most follow.

clue.text: Stone put underground, shifting the odd bits around

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, change places while the rest stay put

parts.note: to bury is to put in the ground

explanation.surface: Burying a stone and then digging it back up in places.
explanation.walkthrough: In BURY the odd letters are B and R; 'shifting the odd bits around' swaps them, turning BUR round to RUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red gemstone, a precious stone.

clue.text: Reason to be upset following small change in role

parts.note: P stands for a penny, small change

indicators.note: to be upset means knocked over and jumbled

explanation.surface: An actor gets upset at a minor tweak to their part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be upset' is the anagram signal, making ERSONA; 'following' places it after the penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona is a character or role someone adopts or plays.

clue.text: Races broadcast interrupted by races broadcast

indicators.note: interrupted by means the next item breaks into the first
broadcast means sown or flung widely, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A sports channel's race coverage is cut into by more race coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'races broadcast' plays three roles: an anagram signal on Races (giving SCAER), the Isle of Man motorcycle races, and the definition. 'interrupted by' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to fling it widely by hand across a field.
